what: Author rulings the Gate 6 harness applies IN MEMORY until the workbook carries them. Nothing here writes to the workbook. R6-1_required_subject.rule: A predicate is satisfied when the passage asserts it of the Son or the Holy Spirit AS DIVINE. Christ's human nature stays excluded.
R6-1_required_subject.supersede_with: Inherited 57: a 'Required subject' column (all 57 families; these five retyped). Until then registry.subject_scope() derives the other 52.

RNR-H06.ruling_example: "the Lord, the giver of life" — Lord, of the Spirit
RNR-H06.required_subject: GOD (the one God: the Father, or the Son or the Holy Spirit where the passage asserts the predicate of that person as divine — e.g. "the Lord, the giver of life" of the Spirit; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature as such)

R6-2_hedged_partial.rule: If the verifier's own floor_reason states that the passage does not assert the predicate, the floor is WORD_ONLY. PARTIAL is for a passage that asserts the predicate INCOMPLETELY, never for one that asserts a NEIGHBOURING proposition.

R6-4_one_text_one_slot.rule: A candidate whose phrase is textually identical — after case folding and whitespace and punctuation normalisation — to one already seated on the card takes no slot, regardless of speaks_for group. It is recorded on the card as a parallel witness with its own registry_id and speaks_for.

same_text_rows.note: Rows that publish ONE text with DIFFERENT wording, so the textual guard cannot see them. Where both survive on a card the named row takes the slot and the other is recorded as a parallel witness, whatever the wording (Eastern Orthodox launch prompt, Task 2d: 'the higher-tier resolution takes the slot').
